# Ensure every Main Street card has dedicated card art (1024×1024 source)

## Problem statement

Every Main Street card renders a square art zone in its top-left corner, but
**108 of the 171 unique cards in `card-data.csv` currently render the same
generic `Fallback` sprite**, so the bulk of the deck is visually
indistinguishable. A player cannot tell an `Upgrade to Patisserie` from a
`Chef` from a `Rainy Day` at a glance, which undermines the 64×64 left-art
redesign's whole purpose.

## Users

- **Player (market / hand / street):** needs to recognise a card by its art
  without reading the title — especially when cards overlap in hand or stack
  on the street.
- **Content author:** needs a documented, testable rule for what art a card
  resolves to, so new cards cannot silently reintroduce `Fallback` art.
- **Engine maintainer:** needs one art-resolution path shared by the runtime
  generator and the static SVG exporter, guarded by a regression test.

User stories:

- As a player, when I look at the market, I can tell any two cards apart by
  their art alone.
- As an upgrade card, I show the art of the business I enhance under my new
  display name, so my purpose is obvious.
- As a content author, when I add a card to `card-data.csv`, the test suite
  tells me if I forgot to give it art.

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-26)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q1 | Art scope / strategy | **Option A — reuse-first.** Actively **duplicate the existing art under the new (card/display) name**, and produce **new art only where necessary** (no suitable existing art). |
| Q2 | Art production ownership | **The producer will produce the new sprites.** This item still owns the mapping, resolver, regeneration tooling and the drift guard. |
| Q3 | Event mapping granularity | **Map events by `trigger` × `targetSynergy` category** (a documented, generated mapping). |

## Producer decisions (answered 2026-09-29)

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|----------|----------|
| Q4 | Source-art size | The producer provides **1024×1024** source art (`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`). The “64×64” is the on-card display zone, not the production size. |
| Q5 | Staff art granularity | **One sprite per staff role** (24 sprites). |
| Q6 | Event-category art | **Unique (bespoke) sprite per `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category** — representatives are not reused. |
| Q7 | Drift-guard tightening | **Yes** — tighten the guard to a strict “zero `Fallback` for every card in `card-data.csv`” assertion once the sprites land, in the same change. |
| Q8 | Duplicate-name clash | **Rename to remove the clashes**: business `Florist` → `Flower Shop`; event `Community Garden` → `Garden Party`. |

Art-production ownership (Q2, 2026-09-26) is unchanged: the producer supplies
all new source sprites.

## Existing state (verified 2026-09-26, `dev` @ 933644bc)

Resolution path (all four card families call it with the card's `name`):

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` → `resolveCardArtName()` /
  `hasDedicatedCardArt()`: (1) spelling alias → (2) exact name → (3)
  `Fallback`.
- Map built by `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs`
  from committed `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` files into
  `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json`.
- A second consumer, `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`,
  duplicates the alias/lookup logic and must be kept in step.

Verified counts:

- `card-data.csv`: **173 rows / 171 unique names** (duplicate names across
  families: `Florist` = business + staff, `Community Garden` = community-space
  + event → name-keyed resolution shares one sprite).
- Committed sprites: **62 dedicated + `Fallback`** (63 map entries).
- Cards resolving today: **65** (63 exact + 2 via aliases).
- **Cards rendering `Fallback`: 108**:

| Family              | Cards | Resolving | Missing |
|---------------------|------:|----------:|--------:|
| business            |    30 |        28 |       2 |
| community-space     |     8 |         1 |       7 |
| upgrade             |    39 |         0 |      39 |
| staff               |    25 |         1 |      24 |
| event               |    71 |        35 |      36 |
| **Total**           |  **173** | **65** | **108** |

Every missing card already has an `art_notes` description in `card-data.csv`
(the source the existing 1024×1024 sprites were built from). There is **no
in-repo image generator** — the existing sprites were committed out-of-band
(commit `05026750`), and the producer will continue producing new art the same
way.

## Size clarification (reviewed 2026-09-29)

The “64×64” in the original title is the **on-card display zone** — a layout
dimension in SVG user units — **not** the size of the source art to produce.
Code review of the generator and renderer confirms three distinct layers:

| Layer | Size | Where | Role |
|-------|-----:|-------|------|
| On-card art zone | 64×64 | `src/scenes/MainStreetCardSvgGenerator.ts` (`GRAPHIC_*`) | SVG layout box only |
| Embedded bitmap | 256×256 | `src/card-art-map.json` (`artResolution`) | WebP `data:` URI in the SVG |
| **Source art** | **1024×1024** | `src/sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` | Generator input |

`src/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` only loads files named
`<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` (`SOURCE_SUFFIX = '_1024_x_1024.png'`) and downscales
each to 256×256 WebP (`ART_RESOLUTION = 256`). Phaser rasterises the card SVG
at `qualityScale = max(4, dpr)`, so the 64×64 zone needs a ≥256×256 bitmap to
stay crisp; a 64×64 source would be stretched ~4× and appear pixelated.

**Produce every new sprite at 1024×1024**, named `<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`, in
`src/sprites/`. The legacy `<Name>_64_x_64.png` files are superseded
thumbnails and are not read by the generator.

## Progress (2026-09-29)

The mapping/resolver/tooling + pending-aware drift guard landed on `dev` as
commit `4b80741` (full unit suite green): `src/card-art-map.json` is now
`version: 3`. Real coverage rose from **65 → 95 of 171** unique cards.

**Duplicate names split (commit `874f419`).** On producer decision Q8 the two
duplicate card names were renamed, so all **173 card names are now unique**:

- business `Florist` → **`Flower Shop`** — keeps the existing rose sprite
  (renamed `Flower Shop_1024_x_1024.png`); its `upgradePath` and
  `Upgrade to Garden Center`'s `targetBusiness` both follow.
- event `Community Garden` → **`Garden Party`** — now needs its own art and maps
  to the `Investment__` category until then.
- staff `Florist` keeps its name; its business restriction is now
  `Flower Shop|Commerce|Culture`.

Card IDs are intentionally unchanged (`biz-florist`, `evt-community-garden`) to
preserve save/challenge compatibility. After the split, **95 of 173** cards
resolve and **78** still render `Fallback`: the staff `Florist` and event
`Garden Party` joined the pending set, giving **46 distinct source sprites** to
produce.

## Desired change (confirmed strategy)

1. **Upgrades (39) — duplicate target art under the new display name.**
   For each `Upgrade to …`, copy the art of its `targetBusiness` to a new
   source sprite named after the upgrade's `newDisplayName` (all 39 are
   distinct, no collisions, and none is already a sprite). Seven targets are
   themselves gaps, so their art must be produced first: `Cafe`,
   `Health Kiosk`, `Laundromat`, `Library`, `Park`, `Playground`,
   `Town Fountain`.
2. **Business / community-space gaps (9) — new art.** `Laundromat`, `Cafe` and
   all community spaces except `Community Garden`: `Park`, `Library`,
   `Playground`, `Town Fountain`, `Health Kiosk`, `Community Shelter`,
   `Public Art`.
3. **Staff (25) — new staff art.** **One sprite per staff role** (confirmed
   2026-09-29), produced by the producer. The split moved `Florist` (staff)
   off the shared business sprite, so all 25 roles need art.
4. **Events (37) — category mapping.** Map each event to a category sprite
   keyed by `(trigger, targetSynergy)`; **unique (bespoke) art per category**
   (confirmed 2026-09-29), produced by the producer. `Garden Party` joined the
   category-mapped set after the split.
5. **Resolver / map.** Extend the generated mapping (and/or `CARD_ART_ALIASES`)
   so both consumers agree and regeneration stays deterministic; keep
   `Fallback` only as the genuine last resort.
6. **Drift guard.** Add a unit test over `card-data.csv` asserting full
   coverage and failing when a new art-less card appears.

## Required art (derived)

| Group | Cards | Mechanism | New sprites |
|-------|------:|-----------|------------:|
| Upgrade | 39 | Duplicate `targetBusiness` art under each upgrade's `newDisplayName` | 0 new (39 copies) |
| Business + community-space gaps | 9 | New source art | 9 |
| Staff | 25 | New source art — one per role | 25 |
| Event | 37 | Unique `(trigger × targetSynergy)` category art — 12 categories | 12 |
| **Total distinct source sprites** | | | **46** |

Event categories for the 36 missing events (representative = an event with
dedicated art today in the same category, available to duplicate):

| `trigger` | `targetSynergy` | Cards | Existing representative |
|-----------|-----------------|------:|-------------------------|
| Incident  | (none)          | 9 | Tax Audit |
| Incident  | Culture         | 1 | Cultural Grant |
| Incident  | Entertainment   | 1 | Noise Complaint |
| Incident  | Food            | 6 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Health          | 1 | *(none — new)* |
| Incident  | Service         | 4 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| (none)          | 3 | Charity Drive |
| Investment| Commerce        | 1 | Grand Opening Sale |
| Investment| Entertainment   | 3 | Street Performer |
| Investment| Food            | 2 | Harvest Festival |
| Investment| Health          | 3 | *(none — new)* |
| Investment| Service         | 2 | *(none — new)* |

Existing dedicated event art (35 events) is retained; only the 36 missing
events are category-mapped. **The producer confirmed on 2026-09-29 that each of
the 12 categories gets unique (bespoke) art** — the “existing representative”
column above is informational only and is not reused.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every **unique** card name in `card-data.csv` resolves via
   `MainStreetCardArt.hasDedicatedCardArt()` to a **non-`Fallback`** sprite
   (documented alias/category mapping counts); currently 65/171.
2. All 39 upgrade cards resolve to art duplicated from their `targetBusiness`
   under the upgrade's `newDisplayName`; no upgrade renders `Fallback`.
3. All 24 staff cards resolve to dedicated staff art; no staff card renders
   `Fallback`.
4. All 36 missing event cards resolve to a documented
   `(trigger, targetSynergy)` category sprite; no event card renders `Fallback`.
5. All 9 business / community-space gaps resolve to dedicated art; no card in
   either family renders `Fallback`.
6. A unit-test drift guard over `card-data.csv` asserts AC 1–5 and fails when a
   new card is added without art; `Fallback` remains in the map and resolver for
   genuinely-unknown/future cards (the existing "unknown card" test still passes).
7. Both consumers of `card-art-map.json` (runtime `MainStreetCardArt.ts` and
   `scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs`) apply the identical mapping;
   regeneration via `scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` is
   deterministic and reproducible.
8. `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` and `public/assets/CREDITS.md`
   document the mapping rules and the licence/attribution of any new art.
9. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
10. `npm run build` is green and the **full project test suite must pass** with
    the new changes.

## Constraints

- New art must be permissively licensed (CC0 / MIT / Apache 2.0) and attributed
  in `public/assets/CREDITS.md`.
- Source art remains `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png`; `card-art-map.json`
  stays generated (never hand-edited).
- No change to the 64×64 zone geometry, the 140×80 card size, the 256×256
  embedded WebP format, or the SVG being self-contained (inline `data:` URI).
- Mapping logic must be expressed once and consumed by both the runtime and the
  static generator.

## Desired artefacts

- Up to 45 new `sprites/<Name>_1024_x_1024.png` source files (9 business /
  community-space, 24 staff, up to 12 event categories) and 39 upgrade
  duplicates named by `newDisplayName`.
- Updated generated mapping + resolver.
- Drift-guard unit test in `tests/main-street/`.
- Docs + credits updates.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `example-games/main-street/MainStreetCardArt.ts` — resolver: targetBusiness /
  category resolution or extended alias path.
- `example-games/main-street/card-art-map.json` — regenerated mapping (data).
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-art.mjs` —
  derive the upgrade-duplication and event-category mapping from
  `card-data.csv` + sprites.
- `example-games/main-street/scripts/generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` —
  second consumer; mirror the mapping.
- `example-games/main-street/sprites/` — new + duplicated `_1024_x_1024.png`
  source art (producer).
- `tests/main-street/card-art.test.ts` — add the `card-data.csv` drift guard.
- `docs/main-street/card-dimensions.md` — document mapping rules.
- `public/assets/CREDITS.md` — licence/attribution for new art.

## Risks / assumptions

- **Art-availability dependency:** the resolver/tooling can land independently,
  but AC 1–5 cannot pass until the producer's sprites are committed. Plan
  should sequence tooling + drift guard first, art last.
- **Duplicate-name collision (resolved 2026-09-29):** the business `Florist`
  and the event `Community Garden` were renamed to `Flower Shop` and
  `Garden Party` (Q8), so every card name is now unique and no sprite is shared
  across families. IDs are unchanged for save/challenge compatibility.
- **Category-art fidelity (resolved 2026-09-29):** the producer confirmed
  unique (bespoke) art for all 12 event categories, so no representative
  sprite is reused.
- **Dual-consumer drift risk:** `generate-main-street-card-svgs.mjs` duplicates
  the alias logic; a mapping change that misses it silently diverges — assert
  both in tests.
- **Scope-creep risk:** "improve the existing 62 sprites" and "redesign the art
  zone" are out of scope — record separately if they surface.
- **Assumption:** `hasDedicatedCardArt()` remains name-keyed; any targetBusiness
  indirection is baked into the generated map so the public API is unchanged.

## Out of scope

- Changing the 64×64 left-art geometry or the 140×80 card dimensions.
- New card types or `card-data.csv` content changes (beyond `art_notes` if new
  art needs them).
- Filling the empty gameplay `description` column on the 45 `event` rows
  (unrelated to art; all 173 rows already carry `art_notes`).
- Redesigning/replacing the existing 62 dedicated sprites.
- Adding an in-repo image-generation tool (the producer supplies the art).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

- Q1 "Art scope / strategy: how much new art vs. mapping/reuse for the 108
  cards?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):** Option A — actively duplicate
  the current art using the new name; new art where necessary. Source:
  interactive producer reply.
- Q2 "Art production ownership & pipeline: who produces the new sprites, and
  does this item ship mapping machinery first?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-26):** "I will produce them." Source: interactive producer reply.
  Research: no in-repo sprite generator exists (last sprite commit
  `05026750`, external).
- Q3 "Event mapping granularity: what taxonomy, and is a category sprite
  acceptable for AC4?" — **Answer (producer, 2026-09-26):**
  `trigger` × `targetSynergy` categories. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q1 prior/open record superseded by the answers above (was OPEN QUESTION).
- Q4 "Source-art size: 64×64 or 1024×1024?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** the producer provides **1024×1024** source art; the 64×64 is
  the on-card display zone. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q5 "Staff art granularity: per-role or shared?" — **Answer (producer,
  2026-09-29):** **one sprite per role**. Source: interactive producer reply.
- Q6 "Event-category art: reuse a representative or unique?" — **Answer
  (producer, 2026-09-29):** **unique** per category. Source: interactive
  producer reply.
- Q7 "Tighten the drift guard to strict zero-`Fallback` once art lands?" —
  **Answer (producer, 2026-09-29):** **yes**. Source: interactive producer
  reply.

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **CG-0MP1QZC6Q005EMEZ** – Asset generation: placeholder SVGs for new cards (completed)
- **CG-0MLTFDAYD0J6KLY3** – Phaser Scene Static Card Layout (completed)

# Remote hosting of card packs (remote bundle source) — Intake Brief

## Problem statement

Card packs are currently discovered from a single source: a content directory
(the Electron launcher) or, since `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD` landed, a bundled
build-time registry (the browser). There is no mechanism for hosting a pack
catalogue remotely, so publishing or updating a pack forces a rebuild and
re-release of the game. This item implements the **remote source provider** on
top of the pack-source registry abstraction (`PackSource[]` /
`PackSourceRegistry`) introduced by `MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`.

## Users

- **Distribution operator** — hosts a signed pack catalogue at a URL and
  expects packs to appear in players' Card Packs panels without rebuilding the
  game.
- **Main Street player** — experiences remote packs identically to bundled
  packs (lock → purchase → enable → deal) and continues to play offline on
  bundled packs when the remote host is unreachable.

Example user stories:

> As a distribution operator, I want to host a card pack catalogue at a URL
> that the game verifies with a signed manifest, so I can publish or update
> packs for an installed game without rebuilding the launcher or the web build.

> As a player, I want remote packs to appear in my Card Packs panel and behave
> exactly like bundled packs, while the game still boots and plays offline on
> bundled packs if the remote host is unreachable.

## Locked design decisions (producer, 2026-10-17)

- **Q1 — Configuration: build-time config constant.** Remote source URLs are
  declared in a build-time config constant (e.g. an environment variable read
  by `vite.config.ts` / a config module), matching the bundled-source pattern.
  No runtime URL mutation in this iteration; launcher-supplied or well-known
  URLs are a possible follow-up.
- **Q2 — Integrity: signed manifests (Ed25519).** Remote manifests are signed
  (Ed25519); the game verifies the signature against a pinned public key before
  trusting any remote pack content. A manifest that fails verification is
  rejected whole (no packs from that source) with a logged warning — safe
  refusal, never a crash. Host allow-list remains as the first gate (only
  configured URLs are fetched at all).
- **Q3 — Timeout & degradation: bounded hard timeout, console-only warning.**
  A hard fetch timeout (≈3 s) bounds the boot path; on failure the game boots
  on bundled packs and logs a warning to the console. **No UI change** — no
  toast, no panel indicator. The Card Packs listing is never empty when a
  bundled pack exists.
- **Q4 — Merge precedence: bundled always wins.** When the same pack id
  appears in more than one source, the **bundled source wins**; a remote pack
  can never override bundled core content. This is implemented by keeping the
  bundled source registered *before* the remote source in the registry (the
  registry's first-wins consultation order) plus an explicit test asserting the
  precedence.

## Scope

1. **Remote source provider.** Implement a `PackSource` (`createRemotePackSource`)
   that fetches a pack manifest and pack CSVs from a configured base URL via
   the loader's existing `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` transport seam and
   contributes its packs to the merged pool.
2. **Configuration.** Declare remote source URLs as a build-time config
   constant (e.g. `VITE_REMOTE_PACK_URL` or a config module), consumed when the
   default registry is built. Multiple remote sources compose additively in
   registration order, always **after** the bundled source.
3. **Merge and precedence.** Pack-id precedence is deterministic: bundled wins
   over remote (remote registered after bundled). Pack-id conflicts between two
   remote sources resolve first-wins (registration order). The core merge
   contract continues to reject duplicate card ids whole.
4. **Gating.** Remote packs remain content-unlock gated; the unlock target key
   and the scoped simulated-purchase flow apply unchanged. Remote packs are not
   automatically ungated.
5. **Degradation.** A remote host that is slow, unreachable, or serving a
   malformed manifest degrades to the bundled/static packs with a warning —
   never blocks boot, never blanks the listing. A bounded timeout (≈3 s) is
   applied to the manifest fetch (and per-file fetches).
6. **Trust and integrity.** Remote manifests are **Ed25519-signed**; the game
   verifies the signature against a pinned public key before trusting content.
   Failure modes: bad signature / missing signature / malformed manifest →
   reject source whole with a warning. Host allow-list: only configured URLs
   are fetched.
7. **Caching / offline.** No client-side caching of remote packs in this
   iteration — remote packs require the remote host at load time; the offline
   story is the bundled packs. Cache in `localStorage` / Cache Storage is a
   recorded follow-up.
8. **Docs and tests.** Cover remote discovery, signed-manifest verification,
   degradation, gating, precedence and asset resolution with tests; document
   the remote-hosting contract (configuration, signing, hosting layout,
   degradation).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Remote discovery.** A pack catalogue hosted at a configured (build-time)
   URL is fetched at runtime and its packs appear in the Card Packs panel
   alongside bundled packs.
2. **Parity.** Remote packs behave identically to bundled packs across the full
   lock → purchase → enable → deal flow, including save/load persistence.
3. **Degradation.** When the remote host is unreachable, slow, or serves a
   malformed manifest, the game boots on bundled packs and logs a warning; the
   Card Packs listing is never empty when a bundled pack exists; the fetch is
   bounded by a timeout (≈3 s) so boot is never blocked.
4. **Rejection of bad data.** A malformed remote manifest or a pack with a bad
   header/duplicate id is rejected whole with a logged warning, without
   affecting packs from other sources.
5. **Deterministic precedence.** Bundled packs always win over remote packs
   with the same pack id; conflicts between remote sources resolve
   first-wins in registration order; precedence is explicit and tested.
6. **Signed-manifest integrity.** A remote manifest whose Ed25519 signature is
   missing, invalid, or not produced by the pinned key is rejected whole with a
   logged warning and no packs from that source are loaded; the failure mode is
   documented.
7. **Asset resolution.** Remote pack art resolves and renders correctly,
   coordinated with `MS-0MV26K321003MWO0` (pack assets self-contained) — remote
   assets resolve through the environment-injected `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls`
   seam.
8. **Documentation.** README / packs README / DEPLOYMENT documentation covers
   remote configuration, the hosting contract (layout, signing), integrity and
   degradation.
9. **Testing.** Full project test suite passes with the new changes; remote
   discovery, signature verification, degradation, precedence, gating and asset
   resolution are covered by automated tests.

## Constraints

- **Reuse existing seams.** The remote source consumes the existing injectable
  `fetchManifest` / `fetchCsv` / `fetchAsset` transports on the loader
  (`createPackSourceTransports`); no core loader changes.
- **Totality.** The remote source never throws: network failures, timeouts,
  malformed responses, signature failures, and missing files all resolve to
  `null` and the core loader degrades to bundled/static packs.
- **Additive.** The remote source is added to the existing
  `PackSourceRegistry` **after** the bundled source, without modifying bundled
  or content-directory sources.
- **Bounded timeout.** Remote fetches on the boot path are bounded (≈3 s) so
  the game never stalls waiting for a slow or hung host.
- **Signing key separation.** The pinned verification public key is a build-time
  constant; the private signing key is held by the distribution operator and is
  never shipped in the game.
- **Pack content stays licence-clean.** Remote packs must satisfy the same
  licence requirements as bundled packs (documented in the hosting contract).
- **No runtime URL mutation** in this iteration (build-time config only).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetPackSources.ts` — `createRemotePackSource`, signature
  verification, registration and precedence.
- `src/MainStreetCardPacks.ts` — remote source configuration + transport
  wiring (consumes the `packSources` option).
- `vite.config.ts` / config module (e.g. `src/mainStreetRemotePacks.ts`) —
  build-time remote URL + pinned public key declaration.
- `src/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — remote source boot wiring.
- `core/src/ui/CardPackLoader.ts` — transport usage (should not need changes).
- `tests/main-street/` — remote discovery, signature verification, degradation,
  precedence, asset-resolution tests.
- `README.md`, `packs/README.md`, `DEPLOYMENT.md` — remote-hosting contract.

## Out of scope

- A pack storefront, purchase/checkout, or pack-authoring UI.
- A pack CDN/build-publish pipeline or signing tooling UI (a natural follow-up
  — the signing key/algorithm contract is defined here, tooling later).
- Real money/Steam storefront transactions.
- Changing the bundled or content-directory sources.
- Client-side caching of remote packs for offline use (recorded follow-up).
- Runtime/launcher-supplied remote URL mutation (build-time config only).

## Related work

- **`MS-0MV1O7EGG004MWGD`** — Make card packs available in the browser
  distribution: provides `PackSource` / `PackSourceRegistry`; **blocks** this
  item (this item depends on it). Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV26K321003MWO0`** — Make card-pack assets self-contained: pack art
  resolves from pack assets; remote assets must consume the
  `LoadedCardPack.assetUrls` seam. Completed and shipped.
- **`MS-0MV0M5BHH0020WFY`** — Add a DLC to test the pack unlock and import:
  parent context for the DLC channel.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk — supply chain.** Remote content is untrusted; a hostile pack could
  inject arbitrary card data. *Mitigation:* Ed25519-signed manifests verified
  against a pinned public key; host allow-list; safe refusal (reject whole,
  log warning, never crash).
- **Risk — signing overhead.** Key management, signing tooling, and
  verification bugs. *Mitigation:* verification is a small, isolated,
  well-tested function; private key never ships; the public key is pinned at
  build time; signing tooling can be a follow-up (the contract is defined).
- **Risk — boot latency.** A remote fetch on the boot path could stall the
  game. *Mitigation:* bounded timeout (≈3 s), non-blocking degradation,
  bundled-first registry order.
- **Risk — offline regression.** A user who once fetched a remote pack cannot
  use it offline. *Mitigation:* explicit decision — no remote caching this

# `implement.py phase_start` records the worktree as `repo_root` on resume-from-worktree

discovered-from:MS-0MVLINWHE004W4CP

## Problem statement

`phase_start` resolves the main checkout root correctly at Step 6.5
(`repo_root = _get_repo_root() or ...`) but then **recomputes it from
`Path.cwd()` at Step 8** and writes that value into
`.implement_state.json`. When `start` is run as a resume from inside an
existing worktree — the normal driven-child pattern — `cwd` *is* the
worktree, so the state file records the worktree as `repo_root` and every
downstream consumer of that value is wrong: `phase_finish` cannot fast-forward
`dev` in the main checkout, and its worktree-removal gate refuses to remove
"the repository root", so a successfully pushed implementation is left
stranded with the work item reset to `open`.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer** resuming a driven child session or re-running `start`
  in an existing worktree: needs `start` → `finish` to work unchanged, with no
  manual state-file surgery.
- **Parent/phase session** orchestrating children: a stranded child leaves the
  parent phase unable to close the epic and burns a session on recovery.
- **Maintainer** reading `.implement_state.json`: needs `repo_root` to mean one
  thing — the main checkout — so state is diagnosable.

Example user stories:

> As a driven child session resuming its worktree, I want `implement.py start`
> to record the main checkout root, so that `finish` can fast-forward `dev`
> and remove my worktree.

> As a parent session, I want a child that already has a bad state file to
> still finish cleanly, so that I do not have to hand-edit JSON to unblock an
> epic.

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (source repo `SorraAgents`; the global
install `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`):

| Line | Code | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 4103 | `repo_root = _get_repo_root() or str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | Step 6.5 — correct main-root resolution (used for the parent-branch refresh) |
| 4171 | `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | **Defect** — Step 8 overwrites the correct value before `_store_signal_globals` / `write_state` |
| 4607-4610 | `repo_root = state.repo_root if state else (...)` | `phase_finish` trusts the (wrong) state value for the `dev` fast-forward, the push and `_sync_parent_branch` |
| 4727 | `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root if state else None)` | Gate 1 compares `worktree_path.resolve()` with `repo_root.resolve()` → `RuntimeError: REFUSE to remove the repository root` |
| 4865 | `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | `phase_abort` Step 3 — same defect class: `_restore_repo_state` runs `git checkout dev` / `git pull` in the worktree, both silently failing (`check=False`) |

Failure sequence observed (resume-from-worktree start):

1. `start` writes `repo_root = <worktree>`; `_store_signal_globals` gets the
   same value, so the SIGTERM handler's `_restore_repo_state` would also run in
   the worktree.
2. `finish` Step 5 tries `git checkout dev` inside the worktree → fails ("already
   checked out"); caught and logged as a warning, so the main checkout is never
   fast-forwarded (the pre-push context-budget gate then works from a stale
   checkout).
3. `finish` Step 6 pushes successfully from the worktree, **then** Step 7 calls
   `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=<worktree>)`, which raises the
   safety-gate `RuntimeError`; the outer handler resets the item to `open`,
   posts no completion comment, and leaves the worktree in place.
4. The worktree can then be removed by a later cleanup pass (signal handler /
   parent phase) **while the child session's `cwd` is still inside it** — the
   reported end state: a session stranded on a deleted working directory.
   `_remove_worktree` deliberately `chdir`s to `repo_root` before removal, but
   with the wrong `repo_root` stored it either raises before that `chdir` or
   chdirs into the worktree it is about to delete.

Live evidence of the same defect (recorded during this intake, not fixed here):

```
.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK-drive-timeout-reconciliation-test-suite/.implement_state.json
  "repo_root": ".../.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK-drive-timeout-reconciliation-test-suite"
  "started_at": "2026-10-24T11:11:45Z"
```

(SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK — Drive timeout-reconciliation test suite — is still
`open`/`intake_complete`; that worktree is the recovery target, not scope of
this item.)

## Desired change

1. **Fix the source of truth.** Make Step 8 use the already-resolved main
   checkout root (reuse the Step 6.5 value / call `_get_repo_root()`), so
   `_store_signal_globals` and the state file always carry the main checkout,
   never the worktree.
2. **Repair stale state defensively.** In `phase_finish` and `phase_abort`,
   treat a `state.repo_root` that resolves to the worktree itself (or to a path
   inside it) as stale and fall back to `_get_repo_root(worktree_path)`; keep
   the correct value for the remaining steps (and, optionally, rewrite the
   state file). This is what unblocks worktrees already stranded by the bug
   **without** hand-editing JSON.
3. **Fix the abort path.** `phase_abort` Step 3 must restore the *main*
   checkout when invoked from inside the worktree.
4. **Regress-proof it.** A test that fails on the pre-fix code: a real
   temporary git repo plus a linked worktree, `cwd` set inside the worktree,
   `start` resumed, asserting the persisted `repo_root` is the main root; plus a
   finish-gate assertion that the worktree path is never handed to
   `_remove_worktree` as `repo_root`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] After a fresh `start` **and** a resume-from-worktree `start` (cwd inside
      `.worklog/worktrees/wl-<id>-…`), the written `.implement_state.json`
      records `repo_root` as the main checkout root (`git rev-parse
      --git-common-dir`'s parent), never the worktree path; the same value is
      passed to `_store_signal_globals`.
- [ ] `phase_finish` treats a stale `state.repo_root` equal to (or inside) the
      worktree as invalid and derives the main root from the worktree, so the
      worktree-removal gate succeeds instead of raising `REFUSE to remove the
      repository root`.
- [ ] `phase_abort` run from inside a worktree restores the **main** checkout
      (`git checkout <parent-branch>` / pull), not the worktree.
- [ ] A regression test in `skill/implement/tests/` reproduces the
      resume-from-worktree start against a real temporary git repo and linked
      worktree (no `_get_repo_root` mocking), and **fails on the pre-fix code**
      while passing after the fix; a second assertion covers the stale-state
      finish path.
- [ ] `_remove_worktree`'s safety gates are unchanged in behaviour: removing
      the true main checkout is still refused (existing coverage retained), and
      the fix supplies the correct root rather than relaxing the check.
- [ ] All existing `skill/implement/tests/` tests pass via the project test
      skill, and the full project test suite passes with the new changes.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including
      code comments, `skill/implement/SKILL.md` / `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`
      where they describe `repo_root`, and any relevant wiki or docs site
      entries (state file schema note: `repo_root` is always the main checkout).

## Constraints

- The fix lives in `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` in the **SorraAgents**
  framework repo (the global install is a symlink), while this work item lives
  in the MainStreet worklog. Implementation therefore runs from the SorraAgents
  checkout with the `MS-…` id; `wl` resolves the MainStreet store by
  prefix-to-sibling scan, and the commit lands on SorraAgents `dev`. Do **not**
  copy `implement.py` into this repo.
- No behavioural change beyond repo-root resolution: commit → push → worktree
  removal ordering, the test/refactor gates and the state-file schema stay as
  they are (only the value written changes).
- No hand editing of live `.implement_state.json` files and no deletion of
  existing stranded worktrees as part of this item.
- The worktree-removal safety gate must keep refusing the real main checkout —
  do not weaken it to make the symptom disappear.
- Keep the change small and local: no refactor of `_get_repo_root`, no new
  abstraction over phase plumbing.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Step 8 `repo_root` assignment
  (line 4171), `phase_finish` state-root consumption (lines ~4607, ~4727) and
  `phase_abort` Step 3 (line 4865) need the fix/hardening.
- `skill/implement/tests/` — New regression test module (real temp git repo +
  linked worktree); existing `test_phase_start_claim.py` mocks
  `_get_repo_root`, which is exactly why this defect escaped.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Document the `repo_root` invariant if the
  worktree/state wording implies cwd derivation.
- `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md` — State-file / repo-root resolution
  guidance, including the resume-from-worktree case.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Read-only reference: this is the
  `_get_repo_root`-equivalent module used elsewhere; confirm no duplicated
  cwd-derived root logic needs the same fix.

## Related work

- MS-0MVLINWHE004W4CP — Export end-of-turn income-collection cap constant
  (completed): the driven-child session during which the state file was written
  with the wrong `repo_root`; that session then died of provider exhaustion.
- MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ — MainStreetScene browser-test load tolerance (parent,
  unrelated topic; this item was filed from one of its driven sessions).
- MS-0MV59PJM5008VBLW — `implement.py` non-fast-forward push recovery
  references undefined `cwd` (completed): precedent for an `implement.py`
  phase_finish defect tracked in this worklog while the fix lands in the
  framework repo.
- WL-0MV533YSW004D1E1 / WL-0MUYTCF4L000FX3M — earlier `implement.py`
  finish/push recovery fixes (framework repo commits `6229a0605`, `a99a6b848`).
- SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK — Drive timeout-reconciliation test suite: live item
  whose state file currently carries the worktree as `repo_root` (recovery
  target once this fix lands; not scope here).
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `_remove_worktree` (safety gate 1),
  `_get_repo_root` (git-common-dir resolution), `_discover_worktree`.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the resume-from-worktree path is the only way to write a bad
  `repo_root`; a fresh start from the main checkout writes the right value
  (verified against existing state files in both repos). Any other cwd-derived
  site would show up as the same symptom, hence the abort-path fix.
- **Risk:** a stale-state fallback in `phase_finish` could mask a genuinely
  mis-specified `repo_root` (e.g. an operator-pointed state file). Mitigation:
  log at WARNING which value was rejected and which was derived, and keep the
  `_remove_worktree` gate independent of the fallback.
- **Risk:** the regression test needs a real linked worktree, which is slower
  and can be flaky on odd hosts. Mitigation: one small module, no browser, no
  test-suite invocation inside it; create the repo and worktree in `tmp_path`
  and assert exit codes/paths only.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the attractor is auditing every `Path.cwd()`
  repo-root derivation across all skills (audit, ship, test, report). That is
  out of scope here — record any further sites found as linked work items.
- **Risk:** the monorepo `core/` engine-sync workflow does not apply (this is
  the framework repo, not MainStreet `core/`); confirm no `engine:sync` step is
  needed before implementing.
- **Risk:** fixing the abort path changes `_restore_repo_state`'s behaviour when
  aborting from the main checkout (it should be identical) — assert this in the
  same test module.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No blocking questions were needed: the filed description already contains the
root cause, the failing call site and the observed symptom, and the remaining
choices were resolved from repository evidence.

- Q: Which repository carries the fix, given the item lives in the MainStreet
  worklog? — Answer (agent, from repo evidence — producer may override): the
  SorraAgents framework repo (`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py`);
  `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`, and
  `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` documents prefix-to-sibling worklog resolution so
  an `MS-…` id resolves from the framework checkout. Precedent:
  MS-0MV59PJM5008VBLW. Source: `readlink -f ~/.pi/agent/skills`,
  `docs/dev/worklog-sync.md` §"Worklog-dir resolution for skill scripts".
- Q: Scope — fix only Step 8, or also the finish/abort consumers? — Answer
  (agent, documented assumption — producer may override): fix Step 8 (root
  cause) **and** harden `phase_finish` against stale state **and** fix
  `phase_abort` Step 3 (same defect class, one line each), because a live
  worktree (SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK) already carries the bad value and would
  otherwise need hand-edited JSON. Source: `.implement_state.json` inspection
  of `.worklog/worktrees/*`.
- Q: Priority — is `low` right for a bug that strands sessions? — Answer
  (agent classification — producer may override): `medium`; it breaks the
  implement workflow on resume and leaves live bad state, but it is neither a
  security/data-loss issue nor a broken build. Source: priority classification
  guide in the intake skill.
- Q: Should this item stay a child of the browser-wait epic
  (MS-0MVK2ACLN004VVIJ)? — Answer (agent, documented assumption — producer may

  Related work. Source: `wl show MS-0MVM7NJF70037YU4 --children --json`.
- Q: Duplicate check — is this already fixed elsewhere? — Answer (agent

## Problem

The ship skill's dev→main release script (`~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh`) runs `npm run build` on the merged tree and then `git add -u` + commit (`Regenerate derived version files for v<version>`) to capture regenerated *tracked* files.

Because `core` is a **git submodule** in this repo, `git add -u` also stages the submodule **pointer**. When the main checkout's `core` working tree sits at a different commit than the one recorded on `dev` (e.g. left at the Tableau-Card-Engine dev tip by another session), the release commit silently bumps the gitlink without updating `configs/engine-pin.json`.

Observed on the v0.1.22 release attempt (2026-10-24T22:57Z):

- `origin/dev`: `core` gitlink = `d907af9f`, `configs/engine-pin.json` = `d907af9f` (consistent).
- Release commit `155eead1 Regenerate derived version files for v0.1.22` changed only `core` → `9ee194e0` (local submodule checkout), leaving the pin at `d907af9f`.
- The full-suite release gate then failed: `tests/main-street/engine-submodule-sync.test.ts > release pin contract (AC3) > matches the committed ./core submodule pointer being shipped with the pin` — expected `9ee194e0…` to be `d907af9f…`.

## Impact

Any release where the main checkout's `core` submodule is not exactly at the pinned SHA produces a red merged tree and blocks the release (exit non-zero before tagging/PR). The failure is misleading — it looks like a pin drift on `dev` when `dev` is actually consistent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The derived-files regeneration step never stages submodule pointer changes: it must be restricted to the files the build actually regenerates (e.g. `git add -u -- ':!core'` or an explicit path list), leaving submodule pointers untouched.
- A regression test in the ship skill proves a dirty/advanced `core` submodule in the checkout does not end up in the derived-files commit.
- Re-running the release with the main checkout's `core` at an unpinned SHA succeeds without a pin-contract failure.

## Workaround applied

`git submodule update --init core` (resetting `core` to `d907af9f`) before re-running the release; the aborted release branch `release/dev-to-main-20261024225757` was deleted.

# AI cost-aware event-choice tests

**Headline:** Failing-first unit tests pinning the cost-aware, presented-list-only AI event-choice contract for Main Street.

Part of **MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY** (cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list).

## Goal

Encode the target contract for `decideEventChoice` before the policy change, so the implementation item is driven red → green. Tests use the existing programmatic option seam (`registerStorylineOptions`) because CSV `options` encoding cannot yet express `cost`/`extraEffect`.

## Acceptance Criteria

# Cost-aware AI event-choice policy

**Headline:** `decideEventChoice` scores only the presented (cost-filtered) option list and projects `cost`/`extraEffect` deltas into the option value.

Part of **MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY** (cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list).

## Goal

Make the AI choose only from the options the player would actually be offered, and account for paid costs and extra effects when comparing them — while keeping the policy deterministic and RNG-free so seeded replays stay byte-identical.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `decideEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts`) considers **only** presented options: when a pending choice is supplied it reads `getPendingStorylineOptions(pending, state)`; otherwise it reads `getStorylineOptions(event, state)` — i.e. the state-aware compile that applies draw-time condition/cost filtering.
- Both AI resolve paths pass the pending choice: `resolvePendingEventChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`) and `resolveCompetitivePendingChoice` (`src/MainStreetEngineCompetitiveTurn.ts`); the existing 3-argument call form still compiles and behaves as today for callers that pass no pending choice.
- **Cost-aware scoring.** Projected option value subtracts `cost.coins` and `cost.reputation` and adds `extraEffect` in addition to `effectPolicy` effects (chain-severity term) before comparing options; reputation is weighted with the same `REPUTATION_SEVERITY_SCALE` the severity model uses, the lowest projected value wins, and ties resolve to the lowest index.
- Legacy binary-choice behaviour is unchanged: for options with no `cost` and no `extraEffect`, the selected index is identical to today's for every shipped choice card (pinned by the storyline regression harness).
- **Determinism.** The policy stays RNG-free (no `state.rng`, `Math.random`, `Date`) so seeded replays remain byte-identical: repeated calls on identical input return the same index.
- The cases from **MS-0MVNU5BRZ0087L1E** are green and `npm run build` (tsc + vite) is clean.

## Minimal Implementation

- Thread an optional pending choice into `decideEventChoice` and use it to obtain the presented list from the core snapshot.
- Add a small pure projection helper (option cost + extra effect → signed value delta) next to `optionChainSeverity`, and fold it into the comparison.
- Update the JSDoc block describing the policy (presented-list contract, cost/extra-effect terms, tie-break) so the code and docs explain the same rule.
- Keep `resolveAiEventChoice` untouched — it already delegates through `resolvePendingEventChoice`.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetEngineScoring.ts` — `decideEventChoice`, `optionChainSeverity`, new cost/extra-effect projection

- `src/MainStreetStoryline.ts` — `getPendingStorylineOptions` / `getStorylineOptions` wrappers over the core snapshot
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetAiEventChoice.test.ts` — contract tests from the test-first item

## Constraints

- No new dependencies; no changes to core (`core/` is the pinned submodule).
- Deterministic: the projection must be a pure function of state + option.
- Resource *enforcement* (actually charging `cost`) is out of scope — tracked as discovered item **MS-0MVNU5M7Z0095CEM** (adapter `applyResourceDelta` seam).

- Reputation is weighted at `REPUTATION_SEVERITY_SCALE` (100) in the projection, matching `eventSeverity`; if the first playtest shows the AI over-avoiding reputation costs the constant can be split later (documented, not speculative).

# Main Street story-line adapter does not apply option cost/extraEffect

**Headline:** The Main Street story-line engine adapter omits the core `applyResourceDelta` seam, so option `cost` and `extraEffect` are never charged or applied.

Discovered-from: `MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY` (cost-aware event-choice over the core presented option list).

## Problem

Core `@story-line` resolves an option's declarative `cost` and `extraEffect` through the engine adapter's optional `applyResourceDelta` seam (`core/src/story-line/resolve.ts`). A legacy adapter without it is left untouched and appends the activity-log line *"Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied: the engine adapter does not implement applyResourceDelta."*

`mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` (`src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts`) implements `rng`, `applyEffect`, `getResources`, `appendLog`, `getActivityLog`, `getTemplate`, `getBaseTypeId`, `getChainScanCards` and `pushChainCard` — but **not** `applyResourceDelta`.

Consequences:

- A cost-gated option is filtered out of the presented list at draw time (`isOptionAffordable`), yet a *presented* cost option is never actually charged — so affordability never changes after paying.
- `extraEffect` deltas silently never land (options are inert where content expects a bonus/penalty).
- Any card using a cost or extra effect pollutes the activity log with the warning line above.

## Impact

Until this is fixed, the AI cost-aware policy (`MS-0MVI0APQY000OIOY`) scores costs that the engine never collects and effects that never apply. The AI unit contract can still be satisfied (projection is a pure function), but end-to-end play with cost-bearing options is incorrect.

Secondary gap (same story, narrower): CSV `options` authoring has no syntax for `cost`/`extraEffect`, and `schemas/main-street-storyline.schema.json` `#/definitions/option` carries only `label`/`successorIds`/`effectPolicy`. So content cannot yet declare a cost — only registered options can. Authoring support should be its own item once enforcement exists.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `mainStreetStorylineEngineAdapter` implements `applyResourceDelta(state, delta)`, applying `coins` and `reputation` deltas to `state.resourceBank` and keeping the ledger/score view consistent (same sync path `resolveEventOption` uses, e.g. `syncResourceBankToLedger`).
- A unit test proves a cost-bearing option deducts exactly `cost.coins`/`cost.reputation` on resolution, for both `effectPolicy: 'apply'` and `'skip'`.
- A unit test proves `extraEffect` deltas are applied for both effect policies, and that the resolution result's `coinChange`/`repChange` reports cost + extra effect + (for `apply`) the card effect.
- An integration test resolves a pending cost choice headlessly and asserts the activity log contains **no** "Story-line cost/extra-effect not applied" line.
- Undo of a resolved paid choice (snapshot command) restores the pre-payment resources; save/load round-trip preserves the post-payment balance.
- Existing behaviour with cost-free options is unchanged (storyline regression harness green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `applyResourceDelta` to the adapter, delegating to the existing state resource helpers and the ledger sync one-liner.
- Follow the settlement order documented in core: card effect (per `effectPolicy`) → cost → extra effect.

## Key Files:

- `src/MainStreetStorylineAdapter.ts` — add `applyResourceDelta`
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — `resolveEventOption` settlement/ledger sync + log assertions
- `src/MainStreetState.ts` — `resourceBank` and ledger sync helpers
- `core/src/story-line/resolve.ts` — settlement order and warning contract (read-only)
- `tests/main-street/storyline-model.test.ts` — resolution test home

## Notes

- `core/` is a pinned submodule — no core changes expected; if core needs a signature change, raise it as a core (`CG-`) item instead.
